words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators take prayer to mean the Qur’an, which contains prohibitions against indecency and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين المراد من الصلاة القرآن وهو ينهى أي فيه النهي عنهما

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects the Qur’an reading because the preceding command to recite revelation makes this sense of prayer difficult to understand.
rows.anchor: لأن إرادة القرآن من الصلاة في هذا الموضع

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say prayer prevents wrongdoing only while the worshipper is performing it, since he cannot engage in either act then.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم أراد به نفس الصلاة وهي تنهى عنهما ما دام العبد في الصلاة

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects mere restraint during prayer as insufficient praise: many other activities, including sleep at its proper time, also prevent wrongdoing temporarily.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد هذا وإلا لا يكون مدحا كاملا للصلاة

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that prayer which does not restrain a person from sins only increases his distance from God; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: نقل عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi holds that a prayer valid under Islamic law restrains its worshipper from both sins in an unrestricted way.
rows.anchor: الصلاة الصحيحة شرعا تنهى عن الأمرين مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prayer intended for God and for showing off is legally invalid and must be repeated; al-Razi compares this with a disputed mixed intention in ablution.
rows.anchor: حتى لو قصد بها الرياء لا تصح صلاته شرعا وتجب عليه الإعادة

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like a servant close to a great, generous king, a worshipper who serves God will not abandon that service to obey the expelled devil.
rows.anchor: أن يترك خدمة الملك ويدخل في طاعة ذلك المطرود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer clothes the worshipper in piety as he stands before God; this spiritual attire makes indecent acts as unfit as filth is for someone wearing fine brocade.
rows.anchor: فكذلك العبد إذا صلى لبس لباس التقوى لأنه واقف بين يدي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because prayers recur, the piety they clothe the worshipper in and the resulting abstention from sins continue over time.
rows.anchor: إن الصلوات متكررة واحدة بعد واحدة فيدوم هذا اللبس فيدوم الامتناع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like an official who receives a fixed seat with a king, the worshipper enters God’s service and should not return to the station of sinners.
rows.anchor: إذا دخل في خدمة ملك وأعطاه منصبا له مقام خاص

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi reads the office analogy as divine protection: whoever prays is guarded by God against indecency and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: من صلى عصمه الله عن الفحشاء والمنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration brings nearness to God (96:19); repeated prayer raises the worshipper’s rank until even minor sins become repugnant to him, let alone major ones.
rows.anchor: فإذا زادت قربته وارتفعت منزلته حتى صار أميرا

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another rational reading, confirmed by transmitted evidence, is that recitation and prayer forbid atheism and associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية وجه آخر معقول يؤكده المنقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi defines atheistic negation as denying God’s existence and associating partners as affirming divinity for someone besides God.
rows.anchor: والتعطيل هو إنكار وجود الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atheism is indecent because indecency is manifest ugliness, while God’s existence is clearer than the sun and every thing bears a sign of God.
rows.anchor: الفاحش هو القبيح الظاهر القبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If calling a wife a mother is condemned as a manifestly wrong statement (58:2), then claiming that God has daughters is even more reprehensible because God cannot beget.
rows.anchor: فالمشرك الذي يقول الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allahu akbar rejects atheism and association: Allah negates denial of God, while akbar excludes a partner equal in their shared attribute of greatness.
rows.anchor: لأن الشريك لا يكون أكبر من الشريك الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bismillah negates atheism; al-Rahman and al-Rahim negate association by naming God as creator of existence and merciful giver of continued life through provision.
rows.anchor: إذا قال بسم الله نفى التعطيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hamdu lillah counters denial of God, while Rabb al-alamin counters association by affirming God’s lordship over all worlds.
rows.anchor: أثبت بقوله الحمد لله خلاف التعطيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting iyyaka in iyyaka naʿbudu rejects atheism and association; the same refutation applies to iyyaka nastaʿin.
rows.anchor: بتقديم إياك نفى التعطيل والإشراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking guidance to a path refutes atheism because it presupposes an aim; calling it straight refutes association because direct worship is nearer than worshipping idols as intercessors.
rows.anchor: المستقيم هو الأقرب والمشرك يعبد الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing testimony that there is no god but God rejects both association and atheism.
rows.anchor: يقول فيها أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer begins and ends with the name Allah, signaling that the worshipper remains with God from its first words to its last.
rows.anchor: أن الصلاة أولها لفظة الله وآخرها لفظة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshipper should not imagine independence from the Prophet after reaching God; his exalted rank depends on Muhammad’s guidance.
rows.anchor: أنت في هذه المنزلة الرفيعة بهداية محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having recognized the Prophet’s guidance, the worshipper should remember his beneficence by blessing him.
rows.anchor: فاذكر إحسانه بالصلاة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After returning from the prayer’s ascent to the community, the worshipper offers them peace, like travelers exchanging greetings.
rows.anchor: فسلم عليهم وبلغهم سلامي كما هو ترتيب المسافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer’s awe-filled form begins with standing before God like a slave before a king and ends with kneeling as one honored with a seat.
rows.anchor: وقوف بين يدي الله كوقوف المملوك بين يدي السلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who kneels before God in this life will not kneel in the afterlife among the wrongdoers described in 19:72.
rows.anchor: لا يكون له جثو في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s remembrance is greater than remembrance of ancestors, whose good qualities people recall with full hearts and voices; it should receive the utmost reverence.
rows.anchor: لكن ذكر الله أكبر ، فينبغي أن يكون على أبلغ وجوه التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted comparison does not name anyone whose remembrance God exceeds; al-Razi says this makes the phrase assert that greatness belongs to God alone, as in Allahu akbar.
rows.anchor: مع حدف بيان ما هو أكبر منه لطيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God knows what people do and prayer is their best deed, they should perform it with reverence.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحسن صنعكم فينبغي أن يكون على وجه التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the preceding account of their fate mentions Hell, it implies resurrection; al-Razi says God does not leave that claim without proof.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر أن عاقبتهم إلى الجحيم وكان في ذلك إشارة إلى الإعادة والحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who created by power and will is able to bring creation back, so the resurrection claim is demonstrated and return is to God.
rows.anchor: يعني من خلق بالقدرة والإرادة لا يعجز عن الرجعة والإعادة فإليه ترجعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse then describes what happens when people return to God.
rows.anchor: ويوم تقوم الساعة يبلس المجرمون

none: This segment only quotes the verse text.

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators hold that the heavens are spread out like a flat plate.
rows.anchor: إنها مبسوطة كصفيحة مستوية

rows.speaker: جميع المهندسين
rows.claim: All astronomers or geometricians hold that the heavens are spherical.
rows.anchor: قول جميع المهندسين

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali sides with the sphere because sensory evidence cannot be contradicted; any relevant report may be interpreted, and scripture does not explicitly require flatness but points toward circularity at 21:33.
rows.anchor: والغزالي رحمه الله قال نحن نوافقهم في ذلك فإن لهم عليها دليلا من المحسوسات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether spherical or flat, the heavens are created by God’s power rather than existing by necessity or nature.
rows.anchor: الواجب أن يقال بأن السموات سواء كانت مستديرة أو مصفحة فهي مخلوقة بقدرة الله لا موجودة بإيجاب وطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On al-Razi’s preferred explanation, the heavens occupy a place within limitless space only through God’s choosing; they have no support preventing displacement and remain by God’s power.
rows.anchor: وكون السماء في بعضه دون بعض ليس إلا بقدرة مختارة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the heavens as a whole have no place because place is what an object rests on; they distinguish occupying a position in air from resting in a place on earth.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم المعنى أن السموات بأسرها ومجموعها لا مكان لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the pronoun as referring to the heavens: people see them without pillars.
rows.anchor: أنه راجع إلى السموات أي ليست هي بعمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to pillars: no pillars are visible, and any invisible support would be God’s power and will.
rows.anchor: أنه راجع إلى العمد أي بغير عمد مرئية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawasi are firmly settled mountains.
rows.anchor: أي جبالا راسية ثابتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean that the mountains were cast down from aversion to the earth’s swaying, or so that it would not sway.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى أن لا تميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth remains stable because of its heaviness; water and winds might otherwise displace it, and a sandy, shifting earth would not support cultivation.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الأرض ثباتها بسبب ثقلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A stable earth benefits moving animals: each can travel, graze, and live in suitable places, whereas unstable ground or unsuitable habitats would cause some animals to perish.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت الأرض ساكنة والحيوانات متحركة تتحرك في المواضع التي تناسبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain is another divine favor whose benefit depends on stable ground: seeds must remain in place until they sprout, or crops cannot grow fully.
rows.anchor: وتمامها بسكون الأرض لأن البذر إذا لم يثبت إلى أن ينبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person to first-person plural is an iltifat that refreshes the listener after a long stretch of one grammatical pattern; al-Razi illustrates this with successive speakers and Bakr.
rows.anchor: أما الفصاحة فمذكورة في باب الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicitly attributing rain to God prevents people from treating it as natural: unlike animal movement, water neither chooses nor naturally rises into the sky.
rows.anchor: إذ الماء لا اختيار له فهو بإرادة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain is a conspicuous, recurrent blessing, so its direct attribution to God should prompt gratitude and bring increased mercy.
rows.anchor: إنزال الماء نعمة ظاهرة متكررة في كل زمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj means kind or species; species divide into pairs, such as trees and non-trees, then fruit-bearing and non-fruit-bearing trees.
rows.anchor: أي من كل جنس ، وكل جنس فتحته زوجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karim can mean productive or generous, yielding abundantly without reckoning, or honored and esteemed, the opposite of despised.
rows.anchor: أي ذي كرم ، لأنه يأتي كثيرا من غير حساب

none: This segment only quotes the verse text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone creates; since everything besides Him is created, people should worship the Creator rather than created things.
rows.anchor: يعني الله خالق وغيره ليس بخالق فكيف تتركون عبادة الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubin can mean manifest or clear to a rational person as being misguidance.
rows.anchor: أي بين أو مبين للعاقل أنه ضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning slightly right or left is a lesser deviation than turning backward; the one who seeks God while distracted by worldly things may arrive only after hardship, while a direct seeker arrives quickly and easily.
rows.anchor: فمن يطلبه ويلتفت إلى غيره من الدنيا وغيرها فهو ضال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who turns away from God never reaches the destination, even after traveling for a long time.
rows.anchor: وأما الذي تولى لا يصل إلى المقصود أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are idolaters who place worship incorrectly or place themselves in the worship of something other than God.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالظالمين المشركون الواضعون لعبادتهم في غير موضعها

words: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشْرِكَ بِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Serving and obeying parents is obligatory unless it entails disobeying God; in that case, they must not be obeyed. Al-Razi says he explained the verse at 29:8.
rows.anchor: أن خدمتهما واجبة وطاعتهما لازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keep bodily company with parents because their claim is over the body, but follow the Prophet’s way intellectually because he educates the mind as parents educate the body.
rows.anchor: صاحبهما بجسمك فإن حقهما على جسمك

words: إِنَّهَآ إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍۢ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Luqman says God will inform people of their deeds (31:15), his son may think secret actions are hidden; Luqman teaches that even an infinitesimal hidden deed is known to God.
rows.anchor: وقع لابنه أن ما يفعل في خفية يخفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a good or bad deed as small as a mustard seed remains known to God when concealed in a secure place such as a rock.
rows.anchor: وتكون مع ذلك الصغر في موضع حريز كالصخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in fatakun indicates connection and combination: the seed is tiny and, together with that smallness, is hidden in a secure place, yet God knows it.
rows.anchor: بالفاء لإفادة الاجتماع يعني إن كانت صغيرة

words: فَتَكُن فِى صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ أَوْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators say the rock is the rock on which the bull rests, located neither in heaven nor on earth.
rows.anchor: ما قاله بعض المفسرين وهو أن المراد بالصخرة

words: فَتَكُن فِى صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ
rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains an ellipsis: the sense is a rock or another place in the heavens or on earth.
rows.anchor: ما قاله الزمخشري وهو أن فيه إضمارا تقديره

words: فَتَكُن فِى صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ أَوْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi’s third answer is that a specific item may precede a general category, but the reverse is awkward; he illustrates this with naming houses of Zayd and Amr and then elsewhere.
rows.anchor: تقديم الخاص وتأخير العام في مثل هذا التقسيم جائز

words: مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍۢ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍۢ فَتَكُن فِى صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ أَوْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence covers four sources of concealment: tiny size, a barrier, great distance in the heavens, and darkness inside the earth; God’s knowledge and disclosure apply despite all four.
rows.anchor: فأثبت الله الرؤية والعلم مع انتفاء الشرائط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying God brings the deed forth is stronger than merely saying He knows it: God displays it to witnesses, joining knowledge with the ability to manifest it.
rows.anchor: من يظهر له الشيء ولا يقدر على إظهاره لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Latif means that God’s power penetrates all things; khabir means that He knows their hidden realities.
rows.anchor: أي نافذ القدرة { خبير } أي عالم ببواطن الأمور

none: This segment only quotes the following verse text.

words: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After citing creation of the heavens and visible and hidden favors, al-Razi says the polytheists still admit God made them; since all creation needs Him, all praise belongs to Him and none besides Him should be worshipped, though they do not understand.
rows.anchor: لما استدل بخلق السموات بغير عمد وبنعمه الظاهرة والباطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also consoles the Prophet: their return will soon reveal his truth and their falsehood, even before the Resurrection, because their admission that God created heaven and earth supports monotheism and exposes their association.
rows.anchor: لا تحزن على تكذيبهم فإن صدقك وكذبهم يتبين عن قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to praise God responds to the public vindication of the Prophet’s truth and the deniers’ falsehood.
rows.anchor: على ظهور صدقك وكذب مكذبيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis leaves the verb know wholly without an object, as in saying someone gives and withholds; another supplies the understood object that all praise belongs to God.
rows.anchor: استعمالا للفعل مع القطع عن المفعول بالكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the absolute construction, denying them any knowledge at all, is more emphatic than saying they do not know that all praise belongs to God.
rows.anchor: والثاني أبلغ لأن قول القائل : فلان لا علم له بكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rationally, everything in the created heavens and earth is itself created; because it is contingent, it depends on a necessary being, directly according to the Ahl al-Sunna or through an intermediary according to others, and ultimately all is from God.
rows.anchor: والممكن لا يقع ولا يوجد إلا بواجب من غير واسطة كما هو مذهب أهل السنة أو بواسطة كما يقوله غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The legal analogy is ownership of land: whatever emerges from it belongs to its owner, so everything within or from the heavens and earth belongs to their owner, God.
rows.anchor: من يملك أرضا وحصل منها شيء ما يكون ذلك لمالك الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First, God is rich because everything belongs to Him and He needs or benefits from none of it; He is praiseworthy for creating it to meet human needs.
rows.anchor: الكل لله وهو غير محتاج إليه غير منتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second, God needs no praise, so unbelievers’ failure to praise Him cannot diminish Him; He is praiseworthy in Himself, vindicating believers and completing their praise.
rows.anchor: عن حمد الحامدين فلا يلحقه نقص بسبب كفر الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third, all created beings are needy and praise whoever meets their needs; only the absolutely rich can be absolutely praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: فلا غني إلا الله فهو الغني المطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hamid can denote one who describes Himself or His servants with praiseworthy qualities; a human hamid can mean that or a grateful worshipper.
rows.anchor: والله إذا قيل له الحميد لا يكون معناه إلا الواصف
